chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariqq, raising it, said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was invited to a meal. When he entered the man’s house, he saw a chicken upon a wall that had laid an egg, and the egg fell upon a peg in the wall and remained fixed upon it; it did not fall and did not break.
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was amazed by it. The man said to him, “Are you amazed by this egg? By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never suffered loss in anything at all.”
He said: Then Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله rose and did not eat anything of his food, and said: “Whoever has not been afflicted with loss, Allah has no need of him.”

key_terms.الْبَيْضَةُ: the egg that became the occasion for amazement
key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: need, concern, or purpose in relation to him
key_terms.رُزِئْتُ: I suffered loss or was afflicted by deprivation
key_terms.طَعَامٍ: a meal or food offered by the host
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْزَأْ: has not been afflicted by loss or trial

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about never experiencing loss or affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a narrative in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله responds to a man who boasts of never having suffered any loss or affliction. The narration conveys that being untouched by hardship is not a sign of divine favor; rather, affliction has spiritual significance in a believer’s life. It underscores a moral and theological teaching about trials, divine concern, and the role of suffering.
